title: In Vitro 3D Cell-Cultured Arterial Models for Studying Vascular Drug Targeting Under Flow
protocol: Design and fabrication of a 3D bifurcation of the human carotid artery model.
Choose images from patients or previously studied geometries of the human carotid artery bifurcation.
Create a computer-aided design model of the mold that needs to be printed.
Print the geometries using a 3D printer.
Cut the temporary printing supports from the printed molds.
Use sandpaper to polish and smooth the molds, especially in areas where the supports were cut.
Rinse the sanded model with isopropyl alcohol to remove plastic dust.
Allow the rinsed model to completely dry in a chemical hood for 2-3 hours.
Spray the molds with transparent lacquer inside a chemical hood.
Allow the sprayed molds to air-dry for 1 hour.
Repeat spraying and drying steps 3 times.
Cut transparent rectangular slides/strips of smooth plastic of the same dimensions as the mold frame.
Glue the slides using lacquer to the frame on all sides and from one side, sealing it at the bottom and leaving open at the top.
Apply the lacquer using a paint brush inside a chemical hood.
Allow the slides to completely dry for at least 24 hours.
Add liquid silicone with its curing agent in a plastic plate in a mass ratio of 1:10.
Stir thoroughly to ensure complete mixing.
Cool the mixture for 15 min at 4 °C.
Degas the mixture in a vacuum desiccator until all air bubbles are eliminated.
Place the mold in the desiccator with the open side facing up.
Slowly pour the silicone mixture into the mold.
Remove any remaining air bubbles until the mixture is clear.
Let the mold stand with the silicone overnight at room temperature.
If the mixture has not fully dried, incubate it at 60 °C for additional hours.
Remove the transparent slides from the mixture once it is fully dry.
Immerse the model in absolute acetone for 48 hours in a chemical hood until the plastic dissolves completely.
Use a wooden stick to remove any remaining plastic pieces.
Incubate the model at 60 °C for at least 4 days to evaporate trapped acetone before cell seeding.
Prepare three connectors: one inlet and two outlets for the carotid model (Table of Materials).
Sterilize the model and connectors using ultraviolet irradiation in a biological hood for 20 minutes.
Coat the models with 4 mL of fibronectin solution (100 µg/mL in PBS) by incubating at 37 °C for 2 hours or overnight at 4 °C.
Inject the fibronectin solution into the model through the inlet using a plastic syringe.
Remove the fibronectin from the model through the outlet.
Wash the model with endothelial cell (EC) medium.
Suspend HUVECs at a concentration of 2.5 × 10^6 cells/mL, then fill the model with 4 mL of this suspension using a syringe.
Place the model on a rotator inside an incubator set to 37 °C and rotate at 1 rpm for 48 hours.
Change the medium after 24 hours in a biological hood.
Return the model to the rotator inside the incubator for another 24 hours.
Remove the model from the rotator.
Wash with 1x PBS using a 10 mL plastic syringe.
Incubate the cells with 4 mL of 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) for 15 min inside a chemical hood.
Rinse 3 times with PBS.
Add 4 mL of PBS and store at 4 °C until the experiment.
Stain the cells inside the model using standard staining protocols.
Merge the two inlets into a single 4 mm ID tube.
Again merge this tube into two 6 mm ID tubes, which connect to the peristaltic pump.
Merge the two 6 mm ID outlet tubes from the peristaltic pump into a single 4 mm tube.
Connect the merged 4 mm tube to an oscillation damper.
Use a 250 mL narrow-mouthed bottle with a three-orifice lid as the damper.
Connect one orifice of the damper to the inlet from the pump.
Close the second orifice with a cork for pressure venting in emergencies.
Extend the third orifice (outlet) of the damper to the bottom of the bottle.
Connect the damper outlet tubing to the inlet of the cultured carotid model.
Merge the two outlets of the model into one tubing, which will be the system’s outlet.
Split the outlet tubing to two tubes; one for the closed circuit and another for the waste container in the open circuit.
Attach a plastic clamp to each tube.
Prepare three containers: one for closed-circuit that can hold 300 mL fluid, and two others of 1 L each for washing and waste (for open circuit).
Add 300 mL of PBS to the closed-circuit container.
Place one inlet tube and one outlet tube inside the closed-circuit container with clamps a and d closed while b and c are open.
Fill the 1 L washing container with distilled water and leave the other 1 L waste container empty.
Connect the inlet and outlets of the carotid model as described in steps 3.3-3.4.
Activate the pump to perfuse fluid once the model is connected.
Place the carotid model under the microscope.
Open the tubing before the inlet and after the outlet of the carotid model.
Set the peristaltic pump at 10 rpm, and turn it on.
Increase the speed in increments of 5 rpm every 4-5 minutes.
Add fluorescent carboxylated polystyrene (PS) particles (2 µm, at a concentration of 1.6 µg/mL) to the 300 mL of PBS in the closed-circuit container when the pump reaches 100 rpm.
Image the region of interest every 10 seconds for 1.5 hours.
Open the clamps of the washing and waste tubes (clamps a and d).
Close the clamps of both the inlet and outlet tubes in the 300 mL container (clamps b and c) to change the system from a closed to open circuit configuration.
Let most of the water flow from the washing container to the waste container at 100 rpm.
Before the transfer is complete, press stop on the peristaltic pump.
Close the tube clamps before the inlet and after the outlet of the carotid model.
Capture images of the model at the region of interest using appropriate filters.
Disconnect the carotid model.
Carefully and slowly add 4 mL of PBS with a 10 mL syringe through the model's inlet.
Connect a "dummy model" instead of the carotid model.
Rinse the system with water.
Add another 1 L of water for washing.
Wash the system until all the water is transferred from the washing container to the waste.
Turn off the peristaltic pump.
